This is not an issue of my GPU overheating. This is an issue of my GPU making my room too hot (which I guess saves a few pennies on heating in the winter but requires me to constantly run my window a/c during the warmer months). I have an AMD 7950 GPU. Any suggestions?
Can you get a decent GPU without producing too much heat?

I'm not going to advocate for any GPU, but what you have to consider is the physics of the processor. So, you're running electricity through a semi conductor. The resistance from the semi conductor is going to cause heat like any material that produces resistance (that's how heaters work). So, to reduce the heat you either need to reduce the resistance, or reduce the voltage.

To get top of the line graphics they will be pumping through far more voltage than a lower end GPU (made of the same year). Look at power consumption to determine the amount of heat that it will produce.

You might need a GPU/Graphics Card, if you are playing 3D graphics games, or maybe mining Bitcoin. The rest of the time, a modern CPU is more than adequate. Intel CPUs have integrated graphics which have quite good performance, even on high graphics games.

You could therefore try removing the Graphics Card entirely, and just going with the CPU. Or you might be able to set your system in the BIOS so that the default hardware for graphics is the CPU's. (The cable would go from the monitor to the motherboard, for the CPU. You could have an additional cable running from the monitor to the Graphics card, if you wanted to easily switch.)

You can also change settings so that the GPU "rests" when it is not required to do hard work. That functionality might need to be enabled in the BIOS, if it is available at all.

You might try something really wild and go for water cooling, with a very long circuit (tubes) leading outside your room. :)
The days of using a GPU to mine BTC are long long gone. It's ASIC or nothing these days.
Probably get a recent, lower-power GPU, or de-clock a high end recent one. Modern ones are by far the most efficient and will get you the most performance with the least heat.

Yes. The 1050ti benchmarks a little higher than the 7950 and has a tdp of 75 watts. That is tiny. It is about as much heat as is generated by a slightly brighter than average light bulb. Worth noting, all energy dies as heat. A 75 watt light bulb and a 75 watt gpu may apply the energy in different ways, but ultimately it all ends up in the same form.

How to properly clean dryer lint filter

Incentive to get the kids to do the laundry and clean the dryer filter, tell them you will teach them fire magic:

Get your dryer lint, dip in Vaseline, and pack it into old cardboard shapes - toilet paper rolls or egg cartons work best.

Add a teaspoon of the following to each golf ball sized fire starter (if you are using toilet paper rolls you can do multi-layer by dividing sections with old candle wax, this also works if you want waterproof fire starters - just dip the whole thing in warm liquid wax then let cool):

  1. Finely chopped aluminium foil for silvery sparks. (Kitchen)
  2. White sugar for loud poppy sparks. (Kitchen)
  3. Borax for green flames. (Laundry)
  4. Table salt for orange flames. (Kitchen)
  5. Iron dust for gold sparks. (Workshop/Garage)
  6. Copper sulfate for green flames (Garden supplies)
  7. Potassium chloride for purple flames (Pool supplies)
  8. Magnesium for bright white sparks (Just use birthday sparkler dust)

This should keep them busy for a while and as you get more experienced, you can make and teach more inventive stuff. Use sparklers as fuses, easiest and cheapest.

Just make a pretty firm rule and clear punishment about never playing with fire without your supervision, when I was young I almost burnt quite a few places down due to lack of rules or supervision.
